channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 红楼梦 · Dream of the Red Chamber
item.description: The 18th-century novel that many call the greatest in the Chinese language: the slow decline of a great family, a doomed love among the young, and a sense that all the beauty and luxury of the world is a passing dream.

item.title: 三国演义 · Romance of the Three Kingdoms
item.description: The 14th-century novel that turned the wars after the Han into the great epic of Chinese loyalty and cunning. Sworn brothers, a god-like strategist, and the maxim that the realm long divided must unite.

item.title: 水浒传 · Water Margin
item.description: One hundred and eight outlaws, each driven from honest life by a corrupt officialdom, gather at the marsh of Liangshan to rob the rich and defy the state. The 14th-century novel of righteous banditry and brotherhood.

item.title: 西游记 · Journey to the West
item.description: A Buddhist monk, a rebellious immortal monkey, a glutton pig, and a river demon travel west for the scriptures. The 16th-century novel of pilgrimage, magic, and mischief that gave the world the Monkey King.

item.title: 兵马俑 · The Terracotta Army
item.description: Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, each with a different face, buried to guard the First Emperor in death. A farmer digging a well found them in 1974, and the silent army became the most astonishing archaeological discovery of the century.

item.title: 三国 · The Three Kingdoms
item.description: After the Han collapsed, China split into three rival states: Wei, Shu, and Wu. The sixty years of their wars produced the most beloved cast of heroes, traitors, and strategists in Chinese history.

item.title: 史记 · Records of the Grand Historian
item.description: Sima Qian wrote the founding work of Chinese historiography under the shadow of his own mutilation: a vast history from the legendary Yellow Emperor to his own Han dynasty, and the model every later dynastic history would follow.

item.title: 隋朝 · The Sui Dynasty
item.description: A short, ferocious dynasty that reunified China after nearly four centuries of division, dug the Grand Canal, and laid the institutions the glorious Tang would inherit, then burned itself out in a single generation.

item.title: 道德经 · Daodejing
item.description: Eighty-one short chapters of paradox and indirection that became the foundational text of Daoism and one of the most translated books in human history. The way that can be spoken is not the constant way.

item.title: 孙子兵法 · The Art of War
item.description: Thirteen terse chapters on conflict, attributed to the strategist Sun Wu, that became the oldest and most influential military treatise in the world. The supreme art is to subdue the enemy without fighting.

item.title: 口语连接词 · Conversational Connectors
item.description: The discourse markers that make spoken Chinese sound natural: buying time, opining, hedging, redirecting, agreeing, and exiting a conversation without abruptness.

item.title: 秦朝 · The Qin Dynasty (221–206 BCE)
item.description: Fifteen years of imperial rule, fifteen centuries of imperial inheritance. The Qin unified the warring states, standardized writing, currency, and roads, built the first long wall, burned the books, and collapsed under the weight of its own apparatus.

item.title: 阿弥陀经 · The Smaller Amitabha Sutra
item.description: The shorter Pure Land sutra: ~1,800 characters in which the Buddha describes Amitābha's Western Pure Land to Śāriputra and names the practice of single-minded recollection of the Buddha's name. The daily-recitation text of Pure Land Buddhism.

item.title: 佛经 · Buddhist Scriptures
item.description: The core Mahāyāna sutras the site presents in full: the Chan canon (心经, 金刚经, 坛经) and the Pure Land canon (阿弥陀经, 无量寿经, 观无量寿经). Each linked here gets its own page with full text, line-by-line audio, pinyin gloss, English translation, and commentary.

item.title: 心经 · The Heart Sutra
item.description: The Heart Sutra: 260 characters that condense the entire Prajñāpāramitā teaching of emptiness. Translated by Xuanzang in 649 CE; chanted daily across China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam ever since. The full text, line by line, with audio, gloss, and commentary.

item.title: 必须 · must, have to (the obligation modal)
item.description: 必须 is the strongest of the everyday modal verbs of obligation: a non-negotiable requirement that the speaker presents as not-up-for-discussion.

item.title: 般若 · prajñā; the Buddhist wisdom that sees emptiness
item.description: 般若 is the specific Buddhist wisdom that perceives the emptiness of self and phenomena: not knowledge, not cleverness, but the realization that dissolves clinging at its root.

item.title: 论语 · The Analects of Confucius
item.description: The Analects: a thin book of recorded conversations and sayings that became the most quoted text in East Asian civilization, the entry point to Confucian thought, and the textbook of imperial education for two thousand years.

item.title: 涅槃 · Nirvana; the extinction of craving and the end of rebirth
item.description: 涅槃 is the Buddhist soteriological terminus: the extinction of the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion, and the cessation of the karmic cycle that they fuel.

item.title: 文明 · civilization; cultivated and refined
item.description: 文明 names both a state of cultivated life (literacy, ritual, the refined arts) and the global concept of civilization. The two meanings share a single Chinese word, and the doubling is the whole story.

item.title: 命 · life, fate, command
item.description: A mouth speaking an order: 令 above, 口 inside. The character that holds together three of the heaviest words in Chinese: life, destiny, and the command from above.

item.title: 跨 · to stride; to span; to bestride
item.description: The character of the long stride: a foot-radical verb that reaches from "step over a threshold" to "span an era" to the modern policy vocabulary of cross-border, cross-industry, cross-cultural everything.

item.title: 跑 · to run; to flee; to operate
item.description: The everyday verb of running: a foot-radical character whose semantic range stretches from "the legs in motion" to "running an errand" to "the engine is running" to a small but productive family of escape-and-flee compounds.

item.title: 她 · she, her
item.description: 她 is the youngest character in everyday Chinese, invented in 1917 to translate "she," and the cause of one of the loudest grammatical fights in modern Chinese letters.

item.title: 越 · to cross over, to surpass
item.description: The character of crossing-and-exceeding: a foot-radical verb that travels from "stride over a barrier" to "the more, the more" to a Chinese state name and a national poetic gesture.

item.title: 长城 · The Great Wall
item.description: Two millennia of walls, watchtowers, and beacon fires: what the Great Wall actually was, and why "the wall" is a translation that flattens a complicated history.

item.title: 方向 · direction; orientation
item.description: 方向 is the compass-word that holds together physical heading, life direction, political orientation, and the deeply Chinese sense that getting your bearings: 辨方向, is the first move in any undertaking.

item.title: 跨越 · to leap across, to span, to transcend
item.description: The compound that lets the Chinese language span gaps: physical, historical, technological, generational. The verb of choice when "越长城" is read figuratively.

item.title: 礼貌 · politeness, courteous manner
item.description: The everyday word for politeness: what 礼 (ritual propriety) becomes when it is shrunk down to the scale of ordinary social life. Polite forms, polite faces, and the precise way modern Chinese distinguishes 礼貌 from 客气, 礼节, and the older 礼 itself.

item.title: 山水 · mountains and water; the landscape
item.description: The paired word that names the Chinese landscape: not "scenery" in the Western sense, but a cosmological pairing of the still and the flowing that became the central subject of a thousand years of painting and poetry.
